focus: ADR-0002 node:sqlite, WAL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, corruption policy under one shared DB, schema migration

findings.title: No tool anywhere is allowed to actually fix a corrupt context.db; doctor is contractually read-only and upgrade never touches data files
findings.claim: D8 in ADR-0010 makes doctor report context.db integrity_check/FTS5 integrity/schema-version as a FAIL row, but ADR-0010 line 24 states doctor "never writes files". ctx_upgrade's only file actions are: (step 3) rename the bundle/version directory, and (step 5) explicitly "Never touch user instruction files or data dirs that were not created by context-mode." context.db IS created by context-mode, but step 5's exclusion plus the fact that upgrade's 5 numbered steps (config regen, bundle swap) never mention context.db means there is no documented code path, in doctor or upgrade, that renames or recreates a corrupt context.db. The r4a pass-A review (finding #7) already flagged that ADR-0002 lacks a corruption clause and proposed 'rename-only, name the one process allowed to do it' as the fix, and PRD E19 is flagged (finding #5) as contradicting the MCP-tool-only decision — but neither finding notices that ADR-0010's own read-only contract for doctor, combined with upgrade's explicit data-dir exclusion, means the proposed rename fix currently has NO home in any tool. This is worse than 'undecided': the two existing ADRs actively forbid the only two candidate executors from doing the fix.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md:24 ('Doctor never writes files, never installs anything, and never spawns on a timer'), :28 (D8 row: 'context.db: integrity_check, FTS5 integrity, schema version' — a check, not a fix), :46 (upgrade step 3 renames only the bundle/version dir), :49 (upgrade step 5: 'Never touch user instruction files or data dirs that were not created by context-mode'). Compare v1 precedent: git log -S 'SQLITE_CORRUPT' in cm-main shows commit 9e246a8e 'fix: WAL checkpoint on exit + corrupt DB recovery (#244)' and commit 50aafdce 'fix(db-base): extend withRetry to catch mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT with lossless heal' (Ousama Ben Younes, 2026-06-23) — v1's heal logic lived inside the long-held DB handle itself (db-base.ts), not in a separate read-only doctor tool, precisely because the handle that detects corruption is the one that must act on it before the session's next write.
findings.archaeology: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY 50aafdce (2026-06-23, 'fix(db-base): extend withRetry to catch mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT with lossless heal') and 9e246a8e ('fix: WAL checkpoint on exit + corrupt DB recovery (#244)'). ORIGINAL_INTENT (50aafdce commit message): 'withRetry only handled SQLITE_BUSY — mid-session corruption on a long-held handle (ContentStore, SessionDB) surfaced the same error on every write for the rest of the session. The open-time guard in the constructor never re-examined the file.' REGRESSION_RISK: v2's single shared context.db with 4+ concurrent writers (ADR-0002) makes an un-fixed corrupt file worse than v1's per-agent DBs — every writer and every FTS reader across every worktree/agent hits the same dead file on every subsequent write, and under the current docs nothing (not doctor, not upgrade) is allowed to rename it aside; the user is stuck until a human manually deletes/renames the file outside any context-mode tool. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: the fix must not reintroduce a silent delete-and-recreate (v1's ContentStore ephemeral-delete behavior, which pass-A finding #7 already correctly bans for the shared-DB case); it must pick exactly one of (a) doctor gets a narrowly-scoped write exception limited to 'rename corrupt context.db aside' only, carved out of the 'never writes files' rule, or (b) upgrade's mode list gains an explicit 'repair' action that is allowed to touch context.db because context-mode created it, overriding the blanket data-dir exclusion for this one named case. Either way ADR-0010's text must be edited, not just ADR-0002's.
findings.fix: Add an explicit exception to ADR-0010: either doctor gets a single narrow write permission ('rename context.db/-wal/-shm aside on integrity_check failure, nothing else') carved out of the 'never writes files' rule, or add a named 'repair' upgrade mode that is exempted from the data-dir exclusion for context.db specifically. State which live writer (per Q6's checkpoint-on-close precedent) is allowed to perform the rename while other open handles exist, and add a GP11 case that starts corrupt and ends healed with zero data loss for the non-corrupt rows, matching v1's 'lossless heal' standard from 50aafdce.

method_note: Followed /context-mode-ops MUST-5 git archaeology for every claim above before verdict (git log -S 'SQLITE_CORRUPT', git show --stat on cited commits) in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mksglu--claude-claude-worktree-workspaces-oss-new/59782ff8-a47e-4c71-b562-cf84e79dcf7d/scratchpad/cm-main.
